summary: Provision catalog-driven self-service for ephemeral experiment pods: Slack/Jira/Confluence + RBAC lifecycle
description:
Issue summary: Request a catalog-driven self-serve onboarding flow for short-lived experiment pods that automatically provisions Slack channels, Jira project skeletons, and Confluence pages with guardrails.
Impact: Research and ML experiment teams must currently file manual requests leading to 2-4 day lead times and ad-hoc permissioning; slows iteration and causes shadow IT.
Environment: Applies to internal org provisioning and Okta-managed guests in production identity domain.
Steps to reproduce / current manual flow: 1) Fill GH form -> 2) Submit INT ticket -> 3) Manual team reviews -> 4) Create Slack channel & invite -> 5) Create Jira project with custom workflow -> 6) Create Confluence space and templates -> 7) Add guest users manually -> 8) Archive manually after end date.
Desired behavior: Self-serve UI lists approved pod types, teams select TTL and guest access level, system automates creation, attaches templated Confluence pages, applies naming conventions, and sets timebound guest membership and auto-archival. The flow should fail open when approvals missing and notify security for manual intervention.
Logs / examples: See slack-provisioning-audit: https://redwood.internal/logs/slack-provision/2026-03; sample manual ticket INT-117272 for reference.
investigation_notes: Spoke with MLEs on 2026-03-10; primary blockers are lack of a canonical template registry and no automated Okta group join API for guests.
SRE advised leveraging existing channel-creation bot but extending to pass TTL and retention metadata tags.
Security requires audit webhook and an approval checkpoint for guests with external domains.
requested_changes: Expose a new 'Experiment Pod' entry in self-service portal with three profiles: 'Sandbox (7d, internal only)', 'Partner Pilot (30d, guest allowed)', 'Research Pod (90d, audited)'.
Template Jira project skeleton with default issue types: experiment, data-collection, infra-request, postmortem and linked Confluence space created from template.
Slack channel creation via bot that sets purpose, enforces naming pattern 'pod-{team}-{slug}-{ttl}', populates pinned templates, and schedules auto-archive removal.
Okta automation to create short-lived groups and provision guest invites by TTL; emit audit events to Splunk/CloudWatch on creation and archival.
Confluence page templates with security checklist and data classification tags; create read-only observers group per pod.
acceptance_criteria: Self-serve UI entry available in portal and visible to devs with 'create_pod' permission.
Creation flow completes end-to-end within 5 minutes and returns created artifacts (Slack URL, Jira key, Confluence URL).
Automated TTL enforcement archives Slack, removes Okta guest group, and marks Jira project archived per retention policy.
Audit log entries are emitted for create and archive events with correlation id.
